summary: Established the evidence for the 1962 Eighteenth Sunday after Pentecost and wrote six records into the leaf: propers/retrieved.txt (two optical pulls, 1962 typica pp. 410-411 and Benziger pp. 404-405), propers/verified.md (all ten elements collated word for word at the facsimile's native 500 ppi, against the Benziger second 1962 witness and against the 1862 Pustet antecedent read on its own page images, with each element's relation to the Clementine and its lawful English route), research/scope.md (transmission evidence, passage-by-passage reception matrix, preserved disagreements, negative results, witness register, chronology audit, rights and bounds), research/interpretations.md (three coherent readings, each with two or more checked authors, full element coverage, four senses, difficulty and comparison), research/source-bindings.toml (33 bindings; tools/source-library validate passes) and research/review-dependencies.toml (14 external paths, including the chronology computation's inputs traced by audit hook). research/chronology.toml and research/chronology-annotations.tex were generated with tools/tpt proper-chronology record/annotations --write and both pass --check. Principal findings: the orations stand complete and unnumbered in the Old Gelasian (Wilson 1894 III.xiv, p. 232) and at the NINETEENTH Sunday in the Hadrianum (Wilson 1915 CXXXVII, p. 175), while the four chants stand as a cue set at the SEVENTEENTH (Wilson 1915 p. 174, footnote b) with a different Alleluia - four different Sunday numbers for one prayer-set across the printed editions; the Offertory's distinctive clauses are in neither the Clementine nor the Greek of Ex 24:4-5; and 'Da pacem' occurs nowhere in the Clementine. One characterisation in research/context.md is corrected from evidence: the clipped marginal numbers of printed p. 410 are lost at that verso's inner margin, not at the fore-edge; nothing that record concludes from the clipping changes. Remaining limitations, all recorded in research/scope.md sections 5 and 10: Jerome and Hilary on Mt 9 were reached only through Aquinas's Catena aurea, not at their own loci; every psalm has exactly one checked direct witness (Augustine), Cassiodorus and Theodoret not being reached; Ecclus 36:18 and the Offertory's own compilation have no located reception at all; the Offertory's and the Introit's textual sources are unidentified, with only exact negatives established; no Roman Psalter witness was reached for the Communion's 'in aula sancta eius'; Hesbert's Sextuplex was not reached, so the chant-set's earliest attestation rests on one bracketed and queried footnote; and the Cummiskey English was read in the tracked payload only, not against the 1861 scan.
